A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, training table, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original random-matrix simulations and experiments measuring trained diffusion-model spectra on synthetic linear data, MNIST, CIFAR10, and CelebA.

after.justification: v4 retains original simulations and trained-model experiments and adds estimator comparisons, a nonlinear synthetic-manifold experiment, and individual-image analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix C modifies the spectral estimator: independent Gaussian probes become d orthogonalized perturbations, and the central-difference algorithm revises its negative-perturbation construction. This changes an analysis component; the diffusion architectures, training objectives, and underlying generative procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds a controlled curved-manifold scenario using ellipsoidal synthetic data generated as y = F(z/||z||), evaluated in Appendix D and Figure 10. Existing linear-manifold datasets and MNIST, CIFAR10, and CelebA remain.

E2.justification: v4 Figure 9 adds a direct comparison between the standard Stanczuk et al. (2022) estimator and the orthogonalized estimator on CelebA and MNIST. v1 adopts the standard procedure but does not report this comparison. The analytical-versus-learned spectral comparison is retained.

E3.justification: Learned-model spectral evaluation changes from K random probes to d orthogonalized probes. Natural-image evaluation adds diffusion times through t = 200. The uniform-variance experiment changes from time-dependent spectra to a sweep over the number of variance groups, with equal column fractions and a caption-reported interval of [10^-2, 1] instead of [10^-3, 1]. Together these substantially revise the measurement and evaluation design; Table 1 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds controls testing whether probe geometry obscures gaps (Figure 9), sensitivity to the number of variance groups (Figure 3, right), transfer to a curved synthetic manifold (Figure 10), and consistency across individual images (Figures 11–13). These substantially expand validation beyond v1's variance-swapping and theory-versus-network analyses.

E5.justification: v1 Section 8 explicitly describes averaging image spectra over 100 images; v4 removes that aggregation disclosure and separately reports individual-image spectra. This changes statistical reporting without establishing that the main-figure aggregation procedure actually changed. Both retain 100 matrix realizations for the random-matrix simulations and provide no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The learned spectral curves in v1 Figures 5–7 are replaced by substantially different profiles in v4 Figures 3–5, with flatter leading portions and clearer gaps under the revised estimator. New results show estimator-dependent distortions, smoothing as variance groups increase, and broadly similar nonlinear-manifold behavior with delayed gap development. Individual-image results are also added. These are revised and additional measurements, not same-setting generative-performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 introduces the nonlinear hidden-manifold definition y = Phi(Fz) in Section 2 and Appendix D, extending the stated modeling framework beyond its linear special case. The spectral-gap formulas and replica derivations in Section 6 and Appendix A are retained. Appendix D supplies a heuristic applicability argument rather than a new nonlinear theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and closing discussion retain the same central contributions: random-matrix analysis of diffusion spectra, experimental investigation of those spectra, three geometric phases, and an explanation of resistance to manifold overfitting. Additional validation does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v1 describes CIFAR10 and CelebA spectra as difficult to interpret; v4 Section 8 explicitly interprets their three phases and proposes explanations involving pixelation and correlations among latent variances. Appendix D adds curvature-scale conditions for applying linear intuition and discusses delayed nonlinear gap development. Appendix C newly attributes obscuring spectral slopes to perturbation sampling, while Section 5.4 expands the manifold-overfitting mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies use of the full available image datasets and 200,000 synthetic training examples. Appendix C documents normalization by the largest singular value and usual removal of the first singular value, alongside the revised algorithms. These disclosures improve reproducibility; the training-configuration table, training budgets, and V100 hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Goldt et al. (2020) and frames the data model through their hidden-manifold formulation. It also positions the orthogonalized estimator as an improvement over Stanczuk et al. (2022). Most other reference edits correct author names or bibliographic presentation rather than introduce new works.

P1.justification: Most exposition and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted revisions move the manifold-overfitting discussion from Section 2.1 to an expanded Section 5.4, rewrite Section 8 as a phase-by-phase account, introduce 'stable latent set' terminology, and correct language and publication headers.

P2.justification: v4 combines the existing introductory illustrations from v1 Figures 1–2 into one multipart figure and relocates the single-variance display from v1 Figure 3 to appendix Figure 7. Empirical plots are redrawn with changed legends, additional curves, and an MNIST inset; new Figures 9–13 present comparisons and supplementary analyses. Table 1 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the central empirical validation. Its estimator comparison directly investigates distortions affecting v1's spectra, and the revised estimator produces closer analytical-versus-learned agreement in Figure 4. The curved-manifold and individual-image checks further support the proposed geometric interpretation beyond the original linear experiments and aggregate displays. Nonlinear applicability remains heuristic, and the missing averaging disclosure reduces reporting clarity, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in methodological validation.
